usage: A common everyday noun for a wristwatch or any watch you wear on your wrist. In Hong Kong speech, it often feels a bit more neutral and more general than very formal words.
Use it with measure words like 一隻手錶 or 呢隻手錶. For an owned item, you can say 我嘅手錶, and for possession or description, the word usually comes before the noun being modified.
It is used for both analog and digital watches, unless the context specifically focuses on a smartwatch. If you want to be more specific, people may say 智能手錶 for a smartwatch.
Very common in daily conversation, shopping, and giving/asking about time or accessories. It is a simple high-frequency word that learners should use naturally in everyday talk.
